nodes.intent: Establish approved bounded-domain instruction boundaries before feature code
nodes.change_spec: Create canonical AGENTS.md and pointer-only CLAUDE.md files for Work Intake, Orchestration, Agent Execution, Verification, Integration and Delivery, Model Routing and Evaluation, and Codebase Knowledge from the approved domain map.
acceptance_criteria: Each approved domain exists under src/domains/<domain>/ with an actionable AGENTS.md.
Each sibling CLAUDE.md contains exactly @AGENTS.md.
Every domain instruction defines terms, owned state, invariants, public interfaces, dependencies, trust boundaries, verification guidance, relevant sources, and footguns.
The domain-map approval record validates and its SHA-256 matches the approved map.

nodes.intent: Deliver immutable work contracts and the direct-task intake path
nodes.change_spec: Implement Work Intake contracts and POST /tasks for one unit or a mechanically validated hand-authored flat DAG, including caller-scoped idempotency and explicit acceptance-criteria provenance.
acceptance_criteria: One direct unit and a flat array of units with depends_on edges are accepted through the same application boundary.
Duplicate IDs, missing or self dependencies, cycles, unknown fields, and absent acceptance criteria are rejected deterministically.
Direct-task criteria are stored unchanged with origin=direct_task and source identifiers.
Idempotency replays return the original result while the same key with a different payload is rejected.
Gate 2 remains mandatory and no decomposition model call occurs on this path.

nodes.intent: Provide provider-normalized, role-indexed, fail-closed model routing
nodes.change_spec: Implement the Model Routing and Evaluation domain foundation with the exact approved model scope, capability ordering, role-indexed bootstrap decisions, provider adapters, and durable routing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Only the five approved provider-qualified models can be selected.
Unavailable explicit models fail closed rather than silently substituting.
Builder and evaluator models differ and evaluator capability is never lower.
Routing decisions record role, selected model, rationale, policy version, and fallback behavior.
Orchestrator-side decomposition routing is not loaded from the DAG-unaware Pool Worker package.

nodes.intent: Provide fresh code-graph and durable wiki retrieval contracts
nodes.change_spec: Implement Codebase Knowledge workspace indexing, Graphify refresh, wiki/index discovery, and retrieval contracts for breadth-oriented decomposition and phase-specific codebase access.
acceptance_criteria: Graphify is pinned and preflighted in the execution environment.
A workspace graph can be built and refreshed against an identified repository head.
Decomposition can request breadth-oriented dependency context and receive index revision metadata.
Grep/LSP remain direct precise lookup tools and no vector store is introduced.
Wiki discovery follows index links and retains raw-source traceability.

Controller-owned predicted-touch metadata identifies its versioned code-graph snapshot and records likely graph units and shared surfaces with provenance sufficient to freeze the advisory metadata with Gate 1; workers neither author nor receive DAG topology.

Target-repository documentation discovery follows available instruction and documentation indexes with raw-source traceability; an absent wiki or other knowledge store is non-blocking and reported as unavailable.

Graph/index data is target-repository scoped, keyed by repository identity, head, and tool/index version, and retained only as bounded, regenerable controller cache data rather than Agent Pool product documentation or a shared sidecar corpus.

nodes.intent: Create the separate orchestrator-side Pi decomposition harness
nodes.change_spec: Build an explicitly loaded control-plane Pi package with a spec-decomposer agent and decomposition skill. It consumes decomposition jobs, uses code-graph breadth retrieval, and emits only the ADR-018 flat DAG fields for deterministic validation.
acceptance_criteria: The harness is physically separate from packages/worker-harness and never loads craft-pool.
Its decomposer emits only id, intent, change_spec, acceptance_criteria, and depends_on for each node.
Kimi K3 is the bootstrap decomposition model with only approved fail-closed fallback policy.
The invocation records prompt, model, tool, package, and code-graph revision provenance.
Schema-invalid output is rejected or repaired only within an explicit bounded policy; the model cannot validate, persist, approve, or dispatch its own DAG.

nodes.intent: Deliver asynchronous free-form spec intake and human-approved DAG persistence
nodes.change_spec: Implement POST /specs, GET status/DAG, approve, and amend application flows backed by the separate decomposition queue, deterministic DAG validation, persistence, and Gate 1.
acceptance_criteria: POST /specs accepts raw markdown plus target repository/branch and returns 202 with a stable spec ID.
Decomposition runs on a separate orchestrator queue and persists its proposed DAG before approval.
Duplicate IDs, missing or self dependencies, cycles, and invalid node payloads fail before Gate 1.
Approval is required before any decomposed node dispatch; retries resume from the approved DAG.
Amend-DAG preserves passed work, validates the replacement topology, and requires renewed approval.
Caller-scoped idempotency replays safely and conflicting payloads reject.

nodes.intent: Deliver durable DAG lifecycle and deterministic ready-node dispatch
nodes.change_spec: Implement the SQLite-backed Orchestration core: work/node state, topological ready-frontier calculation, CAS transitions, stable attempt IDs, deterministic node jobs, leases, and duplicate-result handling.
acceptance_criteria: Only nodes whose dependencies have passed enter the ready frontier.
One deterministic attempt job is emitted per ready node and duplicate delivery is idempotent.
Pool Worker payloads contain one immutable unit and no DAG topology.
State transitions use expected-version checks and invalid transitions are rejected.
Leases and startup reconciliation recover interrupted dispatch/result windows without silently losing work.

Otherwise-ready nodes are serialized when versioned controller-owned predicted-touch metadata indicates sufficiently confident likely overlap, without rewriting approved semantic dependency edges; unavailable or low-confidence predictions fall back to optimistic concurrency, and the prediction and serialization decision are durably recorded.

nodes.intent: Deliver bounded retries, budgets, branch containment, and governed resolutions
nodes.change_spec: Implement failure classification, separate retry counters, node/DAG budgets, dependent-branch freezing, escalation records, reconciliation, and the five ADR-defined human resolution actions.
acceptance_criteria: Logic and integration failures have separate fixed counters with downward-only overrides.
A failed or escalated node blocks only its dependent branch while unrelated ready work continues.
Per-node exhaustion escalates the node; aggregate DAG exhaustion stops new dispatch and lets bounded in-flight work finish.
Retry, manual fix, cancel branch, override/force-pass, and amend-DAG are authorized, validated, and durably audited.
Crash-recovery tests demonstrate reconciliation for leased and partially delivered work.

Repeated actual integration contention or sustained measured prediction misses may produce an amend-DAG recommendation, but predictions never mutate topology or invoke amendment automatically; amend-DAG remains human-initiated, mechanically validated, and subject to renewed Gate 1 approval.

nodes.intent: Execute one DAG-unaware node attempt in a fresh isolated Pi session
nodes.change_spec: Integrate the explicit packages/worker-harness package with fresh attempt workspaces, execution-context preflight, phase-scoped capabilities, pinned models/tools, backend fallback, and secret isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Every attempt receives a fresh launcher-owned context bound to node, attempt, repository, branch, and freshness expectations.
Worker startup validates package files, exact models, Graphify, routing diversity, and schemas before paid work.
Repository commands cannot access provider or GitHub credentials.
The worker receives no DAG topology and executes exactly one attempt contract.
Backend fallback remains the same attempt and records all consumed cost and evidence.

Before workspace cleanup, each retained transcript is finalized, redacted, hashed, durably persisted, verified, and transactionally indexed under transcript_object_id, while transcript_path is only a workspace-relative extraction locator; extraction failure records audit_incomplete and cannot retain an unsafe workspace indefinitely.

nodes.intent: Deliver schema-valid CRAFTS execution and independent tiered grading
nodes.change_spec: Implement CRAFTS phase sequencing, immutable criteria plumbing, phase artifact persistence, red-before-green evidence, deterministic Tier 1, independent Tier 2, and retry context transport.
acceptance_criteria: Every phase emits a schema-valid artifact and invalid or prose-only output fails closed.
Original criteria and origin from either decomposition or direct-task submission reach C and A unchanged; C never re-authors them.
Red-state evidence, green evidence, suite path/hash, commit, image, and tool outputs are attested and persisted.
A is read-only, runs on a different equal-or-higher model, and audits tests and code against the original criteria.
Failure artifacts survive compaction and are supplied to retries while transcripts remain indexed escape hatches.

S persists durable learnings only to an owner-approved target-repository knowledge sink; when no sink exists, it emits a structured proposal and does not create a documentation convention automatically.

nodes.intent: Arbitrate concurrent changes through suite versioning and merged-head re-verification
nodes.change_spec: Implement suite storage and hashes, optimistic integration, test-file conflict re-derivation, final merged Tier-1 execution, provisional-pass reopening, and integration-failure reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Test suites live in the repository and every relevant version is content-hashed.
Conflicting test edits cause the later unit to re-derive against the new head rather than overwrite.
The merged connected component reruns all accumulated Tier-1 suites before sealing.
A re-verification failure can reopen a provisional pass and increments only the integration-failure counter.
Integration evidence is linked to node, attempt, suite hash, and head SHA.

Integration records actual touched graph units and resulting contention, compares predicted and actual overlap for scheduler precision/recall measurement, and retains merged-suite re-verification as the final conflict arbiter.

nodes.intent: Deliver idempotent connected-component pull requests behind mandatory human review
nodes.change_spec: Implement trusted-host branch integration, one commit per node, connected-component PR assembly, GitHub delivery idempotency, scorecard metadata, and Gate 2.
acceptance_criteria: Each independent connected component produces one reviewable PR and each node produces one attributable commit.
Commits and PR metadata include intent, criteria result, model rationale, cost, and verification evidence links.
Stable delivery keys prevent duplicate branches, commits, or PRs during reconciliation.
Only trusted host adapters hold GitHub credentials and repository commands never receive them.
Gate 2 approval remains mandatory for decomposed and direct-task work.

nodes.intent: Continue reviewed work safely from authenticated GitHub feedback
nodes.change_spec: Implement Integration and Delivery webhook ingestion, authenticity and replay checks, comment-to-node mapping, ambiguity escalation, and governed revision commands that re-enter normal execution and grading.
acceptance_criteria: Webhook authenticity and delivery replay are verified before domain commands are accepted.
Commit comments map to the associated node and PR-level comments map to the latest affected node only when unambiguous.
Ambiguous or unauthorized feedback escalates without mutating work state.
Accepted revisions consume normal budgets, execute normal CRAFTS/grading, and append correlated audit evidence.
HTTP webhook transport remains an adapter while mapping and revision policy remain owned by Integration and Delivery.

nodes.intent: Calibrate the highest-volume builder routing row with reproducible evidence
nodes.change_spec: Implement the builder-only eval harness using tested historical tickets, N=3 repetitions, production-equivalent tools, deterministic grading, cost capture, and routing-table publication.
acceptance_criteria: Only tickets with existing tests enter the initial dataset.
Each task-model pair runs three isolated repetitions with the production builder tool surface and no CRAFTS wrapper.
Results record reproducible inputs, model/version, outputs, Tier-1 verdicts, latency, tokens, and cost.
Routing changes are published only from empirical results and preserve the exact approved model scope.
Non-builder eval rows remain explicitly deferred with their named grader approaches.

nodes.intent: Make the v1 controller observable, recoverable, and operable on one host
nodes.change_spec: Implement health/readiness, correlated logs and audit queries, queue/provider/disk/cost visibility, migrations, bounded retention, startup reconciliation, encrypted WAL-safe backup, and restore documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Health and readiness distinguish controller, Redis, SQLite, provider, worker, and delivery dependencies.
Logs and audit queries correlate spec, DAG, node, attempt, model call, and GitHub artifact identifiers.
Migrations and startup reconciliation are idempotent and tested against interrupted states.
Retention is bounded and an encrypted off-host backup includes a consistent SQLite/WAL snapshot.
A documented restore drill is executed successfully in a test environment.

Operations cover transcript-object access classification, bounded retention/deletion state, extraction alerts, WAL-safe backup and restore of audit metadata, and cleanup state that distinguishes complete from incomplete transcript extraction and audit.

The single-host Compose topology builds and runs packages/orchestrator-harness as a dedicated orchestrator-control-plane decomposition service, using its own Dockerfile or dedicated image target, physically separate from Pool Worker containers and never loading craft-pool.

The decomposition service receives only required Pi, code-graph, and provider capabilities and secrets, uses private bounded runtime storage and resource limits, and is covered by service-specific health, readiness, and decomposition-queue connectivity checks.

nodes.intent: Prove the complete v1 objective and map every governing decision to evidence
nodes.change_spec: Add the final end-to-end fixture, ADR/spec traceability matrix, reproducible verification commands, and approved deferral report covering the complete path from free-form spec through review revision.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture demonstrates POST /specs, decomposition, Gate 1, ready-node dispatch, Pool Worker CRAFTS, grading, integration, PR delivery, Gate 2 feedback, and revision completion.
Tests cover duplicate delivery, crash reconciliation, logic and integration retries, dependency freezing, budget exhaustion, re-verification failure, and all five human resolution actions.
Every docs/goal-prompt.md acceptance criterion maps to implementation and automated evidence.
Every ADR maps to code/tests or an explicitly approved deferred item without contradiction.
Pinned lint, typecheck, unit, integration, static, and security checks pass.

Evidence covers predicted-touch scheduling and predicted-vs-actual contention measurement, transcript-cleanup success and extraction-failure fixtures, and traceability for the amended ADR-019, ADR-023, ADR-024, ADR-026, and ADR-032 requirements.

approval.notes: Approved with the ADR-034 domain map and its API/webhook ownership resolutions. Execute ready nodes through fresh local CRAFTS slices; use isolated worktrees for parallel writers. Amended by Kyler to require an explicit dedicated decomposer container/image target and service-level isolation/health coverage in single-host operations.
